hypothesis: The best single probe was enabling timing-driven net weighting (c007, +0.423). Building on c004's looser area balance, the strongest available lever in the shown chunks is to make the partitioner's area-balance repair less disruptive to the timing-critical clustering: raise `area_balance_error` further (0.15 -> 0.20) so fewer macros are force-flipped away from their embedding cluster, preserving the wirelength-aware tier assignment that reduces cross-tier detours and TNS.
analysis: The hypothesis did not hold: raising `area_balance_error` to 0.20 gave only +0.039 total and a negative robust score (-0.020), with two of three cases slightly negative. Ariane improved (score +0.059, dTNS +10.6%), consistent with fewer forced macro flips preserving timing-critical clustering, but bp-ng45 and bp_fe-ng45 regressed (dWNS -5.3% and +1.7% respectively), suggesting the looser balance hurts wirelength/overflow on those designs. Next step: sweep intermediate values (0.16–0.18) or apply the looser balance selectively per design, since the benefit appears case-dependent rather than universal.
